int_name: LINCOLN DR & W MOUNT PLEASANT AVE

result.summary: The intersection features a high-visibility zebra crosswalk and is controlled by a traffic signal with pedestrian indications. The environment includes sidewalks and curb ramps, though the lack of curb extensions and the presence of parked cars near the crossing may reduce visibility and increase exposure.

hazards.name: Parked vehicle sightline obstruction
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb near the crosswalk can block the view between drivers and pedestrians, especially children.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the curb near the intersection.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross the entire roadway width without a refuge island or median to provide a safe waiting area.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image across the roadway.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility by moving pedestrians past parked cars.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The intersection features marked continental crosswalks and sidewalks, but the wide roadway and large turning radii increase pedestrian exposure. While traffic signals are present, the lack of physical separation or refuge islands makes the environment feel prioritized for vehicles.

hazards.name: Wide turning radii
hazards.description: The corners are designed with wide radii, allowing vehicles to make right turns at higher speeds, endangering pedestrians in the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Unprotected crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a median or refuge island for protection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to reduce crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised island in the center of the roadway to provide a safe waiting area for pedestrians mid-crossing.

result.summary: The intersection features a high-visibility zebra crosswalk and continuous sidewalks in a mixed-use urban setting. While a traffic signal is present to control vehicle flow, there are no visible dedicated pedestrian signal heads or physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: The intersection is signalized for vehicles, but lacks dedicated pedestrian signal heads, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicle light cycles.
hazards.location_in_image: At the intersection corners where signals would typically be mounted.

hazards.name: Utility Pole Obstruction
hazards.description: Utility poles are located at the very edge of the curb, which may slightly narrow the effective walking path at the corner.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground and right side of the street.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Installation
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing intervals.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle green light.

result.summary: The intersection features a marked continental crosswalk and a 'No Turn on Red' sign, which provides basic protection for pedestrians. However, the environment lacks visible pedestrian signals and tactile warning surfaces on curb ramps, while parked vehicles near the crossing create sightline obstructions.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: A white vehicle is parked very close to the crosswalk, potentially blocking the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians entering the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the side street curb.

hazards.name: Lack of Tactile Warning Surfaces
hazards.description: The curb ramp at the corner does not have truncated domes or tactile paving, which is a hazard for visually impaired pedestrians.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces within 20 feet of the crosswalk to improve visibility for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Install Pedestrian Signal Heads
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear crossing intervals and improve compliance.
